_reviewerNote: O5 is the best determinism/audit story of the interpreter family: the committed YAML IS the auditable artifact, the runtime is fixed and deterministic, and built-in waits cut flakiness. The cost: no runtime self-heal means drift = red test = human edits YAML (medium human effort per release — see §8.7: 8-14 h). The iOS-simulator-only limit is the dealbreaker for this bank's certification tier (real-device iOS needs community tooling; Perfecto doesn't run Maestro). Note the YAML is a SECOND vocabulary alongside TestCaseIR — adopting O5 forks the schema spine, which is why it scores 3/5 on portability despite being OSS. Compare O1 (committed Java, also auditable, but hand-edited) and O3 (interpreted JSON, also TestCaseIR-shaped, but not auditable until materialized). O5 threads 'authored data, interpreted deterministically, artifact stays auditable' — the needle O3 aims for, but at the cost of a separate DSL.
